name: IL-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans D+19, among the most Democratic in Illinois
Biss has raised $3.4M with outside backing; Elleson reports no fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds near 97%
Open seat after Schakowsky's retirement is the only source of added uncertainty
model.rationale: The D+19 district fundamentals, Biss's dominant fundraising against a Republican with no reported money or outside support, and market pricing near 97% Democratic all point the same way. An open seat alone cannot plausibly close a two-decade-plus partisan gap this large.
model.watch: Only a major scandal involving Biss or an exceptional national Republican wave would put this seat in doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jan Schakowsky (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jan Schakowsky's retirement opens a seat in one of the most Democratic districts in Illinois, a Chicago-area constituency with a partisan lean near D+19. Democrats hold an overwhelming structural edge here, and no serious outside force has targeted the seat for the GOP. Daniel Biss, the Democratic nominee, enters the general election with roughly $3.4 million raised and significant outside backing, while Republican John Elleson has reported no fundraising of note.

With no public general-election polling available, the read rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing, all of which align. Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 97 percent, and the Republican's minimal operation suggests little capacity to exploit the open seat. A Democratic hold is the strong expectation, with the remaining question being the size of the winning margin rather than the outcome itself.
